sections.text_helper: Section 49.4.4 "CRYP symmetric cipher implementation" in chapter 49 (Cryptographic processor (CRYP)), RM0486 Rev 4, page 2361.
sections.section_content:
The cryptographic processor (CRYP) is a 32-bit AHB peripheral that encrypts or decrypts
16-byte blocks of data using the advanced encryption standard (AES). It also implements a
set of approved AES symmetric key security functions summarized in Table417. Those
functions can be certified NIST PUB 140-3.
[Table 417. CRYP approved AES symmetric key functions]
CRYP can be used directly by the CPU, or indirectly using two DMA channels (one for the
plaintext, one for the ciphertext).
It is possible to suspend then resume any CRYP processing, following the sequence
described in Section49.4.8.
